item.title: Central North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ACPN50 PHFO 242311
TWOCP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 PM HST Mon Aug 24 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Pearl and Hermes
Atoll, on Tropical Depression Moke, located several hundred miles
south-southwest of Honolulu, Hawaii, on Tropical Storm Iselle,
located several hundred miles west-southwest of the southern tip of
the Baja California Peninsula, and on newly formed Tropical
Depression Ten-E, located several hundred miles southwest of
the southern tip of Baja California Peninsula.

Western East Pacific:
A trough of low pressure located well to the east-southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands is producing some disorganized showers and
thunderstorms. Some slow development of this system is possible
over the next several days while it drifts north-northeastward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Depression Ten-E are issued under
WMO header WTPZ35 NHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP5.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Depression Ten-E are issued under
WMO header WTPZ25 and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP5.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Cangialosi

item.description:

BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Lala Advisory Number  51
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM HST Mon Aug 24 2026
 
...LALA SLOWLY WEAKENING...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM HST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...34.3N 175.6W
ABOUT 470 MI...755 KM N OF PEARL AND HERMES ATOLL
ABOUT 435 MI...705 KM NNE OF KURE ATOLL
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...60 MPH...95 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 320 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...992 MB...29.30 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lala was
located near latitude 34.3 North, longitude 175.6 West. Lala is
moving toward the northwest near 6 mph (9 km/h). Slow movement
toward the northwest is forecast through the middle of the week.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 60 mph (95 km/h)
with higher gusts. Additional weakening is expected during the next
several days.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles (205 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 992 mb (29.30 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster D. Zelinsky

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Forecast Discussion Number 51
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Mon Aug 24 2026 
000
WTPA42 PHFO 250238
TCDCP2
 
Tropical Storm Lala Discussion Number  51
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM HST Mon Aug 24 2026

ASCAT data that arrived after the issuance of the previous advisory 
indicated that Lala has weakened slightly. The ASCAT-B pass showed 
maximum winds between 40-45 kt, with slightly smaller 34 kt wind 
radii than previously estimated. Accounting for some likely 
undersampling, the initial intensity has been set to 50 kt for this 
advisory. The ASCAT data also indicted Lala is centered slightly 
northeast of previous estimates.

The official track forecast for Lala has been shifted slightly 
northward, mainly due to the initial position adjustment. Otherwise, 
the reasoning behind the forecast is unchanged. Lala is expected to 
move slowly northwestward for the next several days, between a weak 
ridge to its northeast and a weak trough to its southwest. The NHC 
forecast track remains similar to the GDMI and HCCA forecasts 
through 72 h, and then weighs some of the global models a little 
more heavily after that for the post-tropical part of the forecast.
 
No change of note was made to the NHC intensity or size forecast for 
Lala. The tropical storm is moving over cool SSTs and through a 
moderately dry environment (RH less than 50 percent based on GFS and 
ECMWF SHIPS diagnostics). In about 2 days, an increase in south or 
southwesterly wind shear should contribute to Lala losing its deep 
convection and becoming a remnant low about a day after that, near 
the dateline. Simulated satellite imagery from the GFS, ECMWF and 
various hurricane models also agrees with that timing.

NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP022026

...MOKE EXPECTED TO BECOME A REMNANT LOW TONIGHT...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM HST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...16.0N 163.0W
ABOUT 435 MI...695 KM E OF JOHNSTON ISLAND
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 280 DEGREES AT 14 MPH...22 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1005 MB...29.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Moke was
located near latitude 16.0 North, longitude 163.0 West. The
depression is moving toward the west near 14 mph (22 km/h). This 
general motion is forecast to continue tonight.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Moke is expected to degenerate into a trough of low pressure 
tonight or early Tuesday.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1005 mb (29.68 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster D. Zelinsky

item.title: Tropical Depression Moke Forecast Discussion Number 19
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Mon Aug 24 2026 
164 
WTPA43 PHFO 250241
TCDCP3
 
Tropical Depression Moke Discussion Number  19
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP022026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM HST Mon Aug 24 2026

An earlier burst of convection appears to have helped Moke maintain 
its status as a tropical depression for now. ASCAT-C data near 2100 
UTC showed it still has a stretched, but well-enough defined 
circulation, with maximum believable winds near 30 kt. Therefore, 
the initial intensity is held at that value for this forecast 
advisory. Since then, another convective burst has formed north of 
Moke's center, but recent visible imagery also indicates that 
center has become less well-defined over time.

All models continue to indicate that Moke will become post-tropical 
very soon. In fact, based on recent trends it may open into a 
remnant trough of low pressure tonight before it totally loses its 
deep convection. Regardless, no significant changes were made to 
the NHC forecast with the models in good agreement on the forecast 
for the next day or so.

 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  25/0300Z 16.0N 163.0W   30 KT  35 MPH
 12H  25/1200Z 16.0N 165.0W   30 KT  35 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
